binding_choice: Conditional distribution of raw anticipatory count A given observed baseline count B and allowed history H. B is a predictor, not a scored target. No likelihood is applied directly to the signed difference.

observations.B: Number of observed lick onsets in [t0−1.25,t0). Nonnegative integer.
observations.A: Number of observed lick onsets in [t0,t0+1.25). Nonnegative integer; sole behavior target.
observations.D: A−B, a signed integer descriptive outcome; ΔHz=(A−B)/1.25.
observations.missing: Missing baseline or anticipatory event coverage is not an observed zero. Apply a common source-availability mask set before candidate scoring; retain missing counts in coverage reports and the required-cohort denominator.
observations.cue_type: Primary/common behavior score L applies to real CS+ events. A real CS− diagnostic uses a separately typed event and is not mixed with CS+ by trial count. Uncued milk has no legitimate cue prediction window.

information_boundary.prediction_time: Cue onset t0, before reading any lick onset at or after t0. Events exactly at t0 belong to the target window; the cue descriptor itself is an allowed exogenous query input.
allowed: Observed B and other history strictly before t0
Current cue identity and onset time, as observed at t0
Declared protocol probabilities and schedule labels provided equally to all comparators
Past delivered rewards, past omissions, previous-session information only if explicitly permitted by the registered split
Parameters, preprocessing and observation-head fits derived from permitted training data only
forbidden: The signed D, current neural response, or target-derived learned-trial label
Whether the current partially reinforced trial will actually deliver reward
Future reward-consumption latency, future sessions, full-query normalization, or future behavior-dependent analysis horizon
A condition-level or animal-level held-out target summary obtained through another task
information_boundary.history_vs_target: Permitting B at t0 is intentional conditioning on a past observation. It does not authorize using A, D or future target measurements as predictors. This is cue-onset prediction, not a forecast issued before the baseline window.

primary_family.name: NB2 conditional count law, fixed across all mechanisms
primary_family.parameters: μ(B,H)>0 and κ(B,H)>0, both finite. μ is the conditional mean; variance=μ+μ²/κ. Positive parameter links and numerical admissibility checks are fitted/frozen without outer targets.
primary_family.pmf: q(A=a | B=b,H)=Γ(a+κ)/(Γ(κ)Γ(a+1)) × [κ/(κ+μ)]^κ × [μ/(κ+μ)]^a, for every integer a≥0 and b≥0.
primary_family.score: Natural log q(A=a | B=b,H), one term per eligible trial. The primary behavior gain is log q_candidate(A|B,H)−log q_baseline(A|B,H) on the identical observed pair and history. No log q(B) term enters.
primary_family.fit: The observation-head family is fixed here; functional forms, regularization, dispersion structure and tuning budgets are selected using inner training folds and frozen before outer scoring. Every mechanism has the same head options and search budget. The condition/animal split and source clock are common.
primary_family.failure: Nonfinite/zero/negative parameters, invalid probability, or missing submitted prediction are candidate failures. No clipping A/D or deleting negative responses. Calibration or identifiability failure blocks the primary claim; changing the family requires a new registered design before outer labels are seen.

signed_difference.derived_law: q_D(d|B=b,H)=q_A(a=b+d|B=b,H) when d is an integer and b+d≥0; otherwise0. This is a shifted law, not an NB law applied to d.
signed_difference.support: Given b, D∈{−b,−b+1,...}; over all admissible baselines the signed outcome covers all integers.
signed_difference.reporting: Report all signed D values and ΔHz, predicted signed means and intervals from the shifted law as secondary behavior endpoints. They do not replace the raw-count primary score.

mathematical_walkthrough.normalization: For fixed b,H, κ/(κ+μ)∈(0,1). The negative-binomial series sums the displayed PMF over a=0,... to1.
mathematical_walkthrough.finite_positive_support: Every Gamma argument is positive and finite for finite a≥0, κ>0; both probability factors are strictly between0and1. Therefore q(a|b,H)>0 and finite for every admissible finite pair (b,a), including a<b.
mathematical_walkthrough.negative_example: For (B,A)=(3,1), D=−2 and q_D(−2|3,H)=q_A(1|3,H)>0. No target is removed or clamped.
mathematical_walkthrough.extreme_negative_example: For (B,A)=(7,0), D=−7 and the same positive a=0 expression applies with μ(7,H),κ(7,H).
mathematical_walkthrough.positive_example: For (B,A)=(0,4), D=4 and the a=4 PMF is positive.
mathematical_walkthrough.computations_performed: Algebraic sample-space argument only; no authentic observations, candidate fitting, fixtures or scientific execution.

scoring_population: All 11 appetitive conditions have this mandatory behavior endpoint; the six photometry-designated appetitive conditions additionally contribute their eligible paired animals to the named cue-response primary. See IMPROVEMENT_POPULATIONS.json.
unchanged_native: Paper reproduction continues to report baseline-subtracted counts/rates, original learner exclusions and native changepoints. This new conditional prediction target does not alter any original panel.
